newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-INSULTS FLY AFTER WOMEN'S 1,500 FINAL.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-INSULTS FLY AFTER WOMEN'S 1,500 FINAL.

text.p: American Regina Jacobs accused Sonia O'Sullivan of costing her the world 1,500 metres title on Tuesday and shoved the Irish runner in a heated confrontation afterwards in the stadium's mixed zone.

Jacobs, forced to settle for the silver behind Portugal's Carla Sacramento, said she was so angry with O'Sullivan she pushed her in the back as they entered the area where the athletes conduct their media interviews.
"Yes I pushed her and I told her: "You cost me the gold medal, you stupid bitch.'"

Jacobs claimed that O'Sullivan grabbed the top of her singlet with 250 metres to run and held on to it while O'Sullivan regained her balance after being barged out of the way by Switzerland's Anita Wyermann, the eventual bronze medallist.
The Swiss runner appeared to burst through a gap that was not there, creating mayhem in the tightly-bunched pack just as they were preparing to gear up for their sprint to the line.
Jacobs said: "I was in the lead at that point when suddenly Weyermann came through. O'Sullivan claim she fell but she didn't. She held on to my singlet.

"One minute I was leading, the next minute I was two metres behind. She cost me the gold medal. I thought O'Sullivan should have been disqualified. Anyway, I had the last word. I'm on the medal stand, and she isn't, na-na-na-na-na."
O'Sullivan, no stranger to disappointments in major championships, did not deny what went on in the race in which she eventually finished a distant eighth.
"Yes, I grabbed her singlet and held on to it to regain my balance but it was not deliberate," she said.

"I was delighted with the race up until that point. But I got whacked by the Swiss girl and when you get a belt like that it stops you dead. I don't know what Anita was playing at. She should have been disqualified."
O'Sullivan made no comment about what happened in the mixed zone, but did not deny it occured. "You have to ignore what
happens in the heat of the moment. None of this is going to affect my bid to retain my 5,000 metres title later in the week."
Weyermann played down her role in the affair. "I saw a gap and went for it," she explained, "I'm really happy with the way it turned out."
Despite the spat and a few minutes when Irish officials debated whether to appeal or not, no appeal was forthcoming from any team.
The graceful Sacramento, running an intelligent, tactically perfect race, stayed away from the bumbing and grinding to win in four minutes 04.24 seconds. Jacobs clocked 4:04.63 and Weyermann 4:04.70.
